content: Indication-specific dosing for P57, also known as Hoodia, includes a recommended oral dosage of 250-750 mg taken two to four times daily (BID-QID) as an appetite suppressant. Traditionally, Hoodia has been used by the San Bushmen of South Africa to suppress appetite during long hunting trips. P57 is a steroidal glycoside that is believed to have pharmacological activity. It has been isolated and studied in clinical trials. In one study, administration of large doses of P57 resulted in a reduction of daily caloric intake by approximately 100 calories by Day 15 in a small group of healthy but overweight individuals. Many weight loss supplements claim to contain Hoodia; however, the actual amount of Hoodia present in these products and its efficacy remain unverified. No adverse effects have been reported in the available data. However, P57 has been noted to suppress thirst in addition to its appetite-suppressing effects. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific category assigned (Pregnancy Category: N/A; Lactation: N/A). However, it is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
